paragraphs.text: White-blue ( or WU ), also called Azorius , is an allied color pair. White ( ) and blue ( ) share a philosophy of restraint; they are mutual enemies of red ( ), the color of impulse and emotion. Blue and white both use the evergreen keywords defender , flying , vigilance , and ward for mana ; they are also the primary colors of flickering and of artifact synergies. The white-blue color pair lends itself to control decks .

White wants to provide for the collective group, while blue wants everyone to reach their full potential. As mutual enemies of red , they share a distrust of short-term thinking and impulsive action. White and blue's alliance is therefore about restraint. White is careful and efficient when organizing society, and blue gathers knowledge and evaluates all its options before acting.

When paired, white and blue strive to improve society for everyone's benefit. White-blue is the color pair of civilization ; it creates systems such as law , politics , and labor specialization that allow for long-term social betterment. It is thoughtful, emotionally detached, and farsighted.

White-blue systems attempt to safeguard society from the excesses of freedom and chaos. As a result, white-blue can be slow and inflexible, unable to react quickly to new problems. However, it can become unstoppable if its long-term plans go unchecked.

White and blue's disagreements mirror the green-black conflict of destiny versus free will. White, an ally of green , believes that everyone has a role to play in making society better. Blue, an ally of black , believes in agency and self-determination. White wants to maximize the potential of the group, while blue also cares about maximizing the potential of the individual. White thinks that self-improvement is a waste of time, while blue sees white's rules and regulations as holding back individuals' potential.
Examples of White-blue heroes include Teferi Akosa and Niko Aris , while examples of villains include Ojutai and Dovin Baan .

White and blue have some natural mechanical overlap: they are the most defensive, reactive, and evasive colors. White-blue decks therefore tend to be controlling ; they combine white removal spells and board wipes with blue counterspells and card draw to stall the game. These decks can sometimes stall indefinitely without winning, a play pattern that designers try to mitigate. Control finishers tend to be evasive creatures.

The aggressive strategies of white ( weenie ) and blue ( tempo ) have less overlap, making them harder to design. The most common white-blue aggressive archetype is fliers , which tries to end the game quickly with flying creatures.
The following mechanics are shared by white and blue.
These multicolored cards best exemplify the strengths of white and blue:
Angelic Shield — White's defensive nature and blue's ability to bounce creatures
Deft Duelist — Efficiently combines evergreen mechanics common in white ( first strike ) and blue ( shroud ) onto one creature
Palliation Accord — White's damage prevention ability and blue's ability to tap creatures
Spectral Shield — White's defensive nature and blue's shroud ability
Wings of Hope — White's defensive nature and the two color's flying ability
